purpose: Development comparison of snapshot admission policies; not final qualification.
checkpoint_selection: Use latest at each scheduled update, never internal best. Pin the immutable repository revision and checkpoint/export hashes before launching each screen.
matches_per_deal: All candidate seats and all four rule combinations.
validation: 2553-fixture checkpoint/export comparison, including strict numerical tolerances; record failures and do not qualify failing exports.
Exact candidate and opponent hashes, counts, seed sets, unique seat/rule/deal keys and paired completeness.
Zero actual-game truncations, illegal actions and search truncations; explicit search diagnostics.
Inspect training metrics for both arms: completed games, truncation, admission mode and actual snapshot updates.

comparisons.primary: periodic_anchor minus best at update19, separately for each opponent/player count; no pooled win rate across counts.
secondary: Each arm versus starting H200 update29 on the same held-out deals.
Separate original/open, original/sealed, recharged/open and recharged/sealed results for every count/opponent.
comparisons.bootstrap_unit: gameSeed, retaining all seats and rule repeats

interpretation: A single training seed is a pilot and cannot establish robustness across training randomness.
Async scheduling does not guarantee identical training trajectories despite matched configuration.
Intervals are marginal exploratory intervals, not simultaneous family-wide confidence bounds.
These development seeds have been used for previous checkpoint screening; they are not the reserved final test.
Report all scheduled checkpoints and comparisons, including regressions. Do not silently select the best subgroup.
No automatic promotion or deployment. Final strength, serving and export gates remain unchanged. Strong search-opponent follow-up requires evidence from these screens.
